data.expected_signal: max errors vs FP64 reference within tolerance for all cases, or a specific failing case

fail: ValueError('all input values must be finite')

data.passing_cases: only degenerate symmetric inputs (constant rows, zeros, alternating +-extremes, subnormals)

evidence.summary: Kernel output diverges from the exact DFT far beyond the contract tolerance on ordinary random FP16 inputs across all N in {64,128,256} and batches 1-256 (e.g. randn_B1_N64 max abs error 14.48 with 62/130 violating elements; make_inputs max error 40.58 with 882 violations). Violations begin at frequency k=1; only degenerate symmetric inputs (constant, zero, alternating-extreme rows) match. Container/shape/contiguity/input-preservation checks passed, so the failure is purely numeric correctness of non-DC frequencies.

rationale: The kernel computes in FP64 with a 65-entry cos table and writes FP32; extreme FP16 inputs (±65504, subnormals, all-equal rows) could stress the 1e-4+1e-6|exact| tolerance, and the Triton gather/bit-reverse pipeline might misbehave at some N/B combination.

scope_evidence.summary: Contract: every finite FP16 value is legal (signed zeros, subnormals, both finite extremes), B in 1..256, N in {64,128,256}, tolerance abs(actual-exact) <= 1e-4 + 1e-6*abs(exact), nonfinite output incorrect, input storage preserved and separate output.

scope_rationale: Contract requires the tolerance for every legal finite FP16 input across N∈{64,128,256} and 1≤B≤256, plus fresh contiguous FP32 output and input preservation.
statement: run(values) fails the contract for some legal input — e.g. wrong values at some N/B, tolerance violations on extreme FP16 inputs, non-fresh/non-contiguous output, or mutation of input storage.
